terms.gloss: adjust, fit, adapt (one thing to another)
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; ad + accusative or dative
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.250: corōnam sibi ad caput (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 9.7: meum cōnsilium accommodābō ad tuum
terms.comment: Fitting a thing to something else, a garland to the head or one’s plans to a friend’s; with sē, to adjust oneself to someone, comply (Cic. Or. 24).

terms.gloss: adjust to the right degree, regulate (heat, a mixture, water)
evidence: Hor. C. 3.19.6: quis aquam temperet ignibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly to mix in due proportion; so to bring heat, water or a voice to the right measure. With the dative or ab it means to refrain from something.

phrases.english: I’ll fit my plan to yours

phrases.latin: Aquam temperā, nē nimis calida sit.
phrases.english: Adjust the water so it isn’t too hot.

sources: Lewis & Short: accommodo · Lewis & Short: tempero
